svg.text: Figure 4. Where the slice-spacing effect sits inside Sybil: a signal from Sybil's own padding
NLST test, pre-registered (H2, H6, H7): mean change of Sybil's logit
as Sybil gives it, and with shared axis 0 switched off (set to its dev mean in all five members; nothing refitted)
mean change of the logit (z-fix minus as read; later minus earlier screen per stretch change)
Switching axis 0 off removes the mean shift, not the exam-by-exam scatter: z-fix exams whose 6-year logit moves >= 1/4 SD (as in H1):
65.7% as Sybil gives it, 54.5% with axis 0 off. 1-year AUROC with axis 0 off minus as given: -0.0003 [-0.005, +0.003] (no change detected; secondary).
The z-fix moves axis 0 by -2.73 dev SD [-2.76, -2.70]; a change of stretch between yearly screens moves it by
2.39 dev SD [2.28, 2.50]. H7 is partly seen before the freeze; 121 of its 134 changed pairs involve GE.
Synthetic z-stretch of 48 contiguous dev scans, 12 per maker (exploratory; no outcome read)
Stretch factor f = how much longer Sybil sees the scan (f = 1: the scan as it is; f = 2: what Sybil does to a 50%-overlapping scan read with the wrong spacing)
f = 1 with air instead of Sybil's padding
f = 2 at the same filling as the true scan
Axis 0 rises with f and stops once Sybil's 200-slice box is full. Axis 0 and A0 rise in all four makers; the total 1-year logit at f = 2 does not in every maker (Philips +0.06 [-0.32, +0.43]).
Square: f = 2 cut back to the true scan's slice count and padded like it keeps 2.8% [2.4, 3.1] of the axis-0 shift (its logit is not read: the cut removes about half of the lung).
Diamond: no stretch, only air instead of Sybil's padding: axis 0 +2.41 SD, 1-year logit +0.245 [+0.226, +0.265]. The stretch is a resampling of the images, not a real overlapping reconstruction.
Real overlapping dev scans: 63 scans (GE 24, Philips 27, Siemens 12; weighted to the dev maker mix; exploratory; no outcome read)
Change within the same scans; each row names what is compared. "Sybil's run" = the scan as Sybil reads it (wrong spacing, Sybil's padding)
controls: only the axis-0 change is read (the mirror adds
image content; the cut-back scan loses about half of the lung)
true spacing minus Sybil's run; max-pool -2.71, attention -0.08
that series minus Sybil's run; 36 GE + Siemens scans
both runs padded with air (-1,000 HU): z-fix minus that run
minus Sybil's run (36% of slice attention on the mirror)
stretched scan cut to the z-fix's length, padded; minus Sybil's run
z-fix minus the cut-back stretched scan

Air padding keeps 14.6% [14.0, 15.2] of the axis-0 shift; mirrored box ends remove 97.4%; at the same filling the stretch alone gives 2.2% [1.9, 2.6]. Every second slice gives 1.003 [1.002, 1.003] times the z-fix shift.
With air padding the mean logit change is near 0, but the exam-by-exam scatter stays (right column): air padding does not fix Sybil, and it moves ordinary scans
out of their usual range of axis 0. Every-second-slice row: GE and Siemens only (the one Philips scan with ratio 0.5 is left out by the rule of >= 5 per maker).
How axis 0 depends on the padding left in the box across all 7,336 dev scans: Supplementary Figure S1.
